symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V\) is the set of observed substantive variables.

symbols.name: S

symbols.name: sigma

symbols.def: \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}}\) satisfies \(2\le |\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for every \(v\in V\) and \(\mathcal X_S=\{0,1\}\).

symbols.name: sigmabin

symbols.name: G
symbols.type: finite augmented acyclic directed mixed graph
symbols.space: ADMGs on \(V\cup\{S\}\) in which \(S\) has no children
symbols.def: \(G^S\) has an acyclic directed part and \(S\) has no children. It is the exact graph induced by the augmented SCM: \(u\to v\) holds exactly when \(u\) belongs to the declared observed-parent set of \(v\), and \(v\leftrightarrow w\) holds exactly when the mechanisms for \(v\) and \(w\) share an exogenous input.

symbols.name: X

symbols.name: Y

symbols.name: xbin

symbols.name: NS

symbols.name: XN

symbols.name: xN

symbols.name: YS

symbols.name: YN

symbols.name: W

assumptions.condition: For the fixed finite signature \(\sigma\), the generic model \(M\) is a recursive augmented SCM whose exogenous variables are mutually independent and whose induced augmented graph is exactly \(G^S\): for every endogenous vertex \(v\), its declared observed-parent set equals \(\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\), and for distinct \(v,w\), \(v\leftrightarrow w\) belongs to \(G^S\) if and only if their mechanisms share an exogenous input.

standard.name: recursive augmented-SCM compatibility with exact induced graph and shared exogenous variables

assumptions.condition: Within the fixed signature \(\sigma\), the generic model \(M\) satisfies \(P_M(V=v,S=1)>0\) for every \(v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\).

The generic two-selector model \(M_{EI}\) is recursive, its exogenous variables are mutually independent, both \(S_E\) and \(S_I\) are childless, every declared observed-parent interface equals the corresponding parent set in \(G^{EI}\), and two distinct mechanisms share an exogenous input if and only if their vertices are joined by a bidirected edge in \(G^{EI}\).

novel.justification: This is an analyst-imposed two-selector exact-graph feasibility regime for combining exposure and imaging margins. AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID defines the exact induced-graph convention only for one selector, while two childless selectors with a common substantive system are realistic for nonoverlapping exposure and imaging cohorts.

novel.justification: This is an analyst-imposed full-support feasibility condition for the exposure-selected cohort, appropriate after finite coarsening to cells retained in a positivity audit. AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID supplies only the one-selector analogue.

definitions.name: positive compatible augmented-SCM class
definitions.construction: For every finite signature \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}}\) with \(2\le|\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for \(v\in V\) and \(\mathcal X_S=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)=\{M:M\text{ has endogenous signature }\sigma,\ M\text{ is a recursive augmented SCM with mutually independent exogenous variables, }\operatorname{Pa}_M(v)=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\text{ for every }v,\ v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal U_M^v\cap\mathcal U_M^w\ne\varnothing\text{ for every distinct }v,w,\text{ and }P_M(V=z,S=1)>0\text{ for every }z\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\}\).

definitions.name: exact finite augmented-SCM certificate type
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) consists of finite strings \(E=((\mathcal U_j,p_j,I_j)_{j=1}^m,(P_v,f_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}})\). Each \(\mathcal U_j\) is a nonempty finite latent support, \(p_j:\mathcal U_j\to\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]\) is a complete normalized rational probability table, and \(I_j\subseteq V\cup\{S\}\) declares every endogenous mechanism receiving latent factor \(U_j\); distinct factors are interpreted independently with joint mass \(\prod_jp_j(u_j)\). Each \(P_v\) is the declared observed-parent interface and each \(f_v\) is a complete deterministic table from the states of \(P_v\) and the incident latent factors to \(\{0,1\}\). Exact graph compatibility requires \(P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) for every \(v\), and for every distinct \(v,w\), \(v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\) if and only if \(\{v,w\}\subseteq I_j\) for at least one \(j\). Thus every listed directed parent occurs in the declared interface, no unlisted directed parent occurs, every listed bidirected edge has a declared shared factor, and no unlisted vertex pair shares a factor. The induced selected atom \(P_{\llbracket E\rrbracket}(V=z,S=1)\) must be positive for every \(z\in\{0,1\}^V\), and a scope \(I_j\) may contain arbitrarily many mechanisms.

definitions.name: coordinate-constant exact-graph completion
definitions.construction: For \(E\in\operatorname{RawCertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}(E)\) adds each missing graph parent \(u\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) to the declared interface \(P_v\) and extends \(f_v\) constantly in that coordinate. For each listed bidirected edge \(v\leftrightarrow w\) not already witnessed by a shared factor, it adds a fresh independent fair binary factor with scope \(\{v,w\}\) and extends both incident structural tables constantly in that factor. It adds no other parent or shared scope and retains every original probability and structural table entry.

definitions.name: exact exhaustive NONID checker
definitions.construction: Given \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) and \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}\) first validates finite-table completeness, rational probability normalization and nonnegativity, the product-factor interpretation of mutual independence, and exact induced-graph equality: \(P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) for every vertex, and \(v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\) exactly when some declared latent scope contains both endpoints. For each \(i\in\{0,1\}\), exhaustive enumeration of the \(R(E_i)\) joint latent assignments computes exact unnormalized selected atoms \(a_i(v)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1)\) and \(z_i=\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^V}a_i(v)\). The checker requires \(a_i(v)>0\) and \(a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\) for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^V\). It then replaces the structural tables for \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), enumerates again to obtain exact postintervention selected masses \(b_i(y)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(Y=y,S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}}))\) and \(q_i=\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^Y}b_i(y)\), and accepts exactly when \(q_0q_1>0\) and \(b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0\) for some \(y\in\{0,1\}^Y\). For a universal implementation constant \(c\), this procedure uses at most \(c\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations.

definitions.name: S-component partition
definitions.construction: For every \(H\subseteq N_S\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)=\{K\cap H:K\in\mathcal D(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]),\ K\cap H\ne\varnothing\}\), where \(\mathcal D\) denotes the district partition.

definitions.name: S-Hedge predicate
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\iff C\subsetneq T\subseteq N_S,\ \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\},\ \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\},\text{ and }\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\).

definitions.name: graphwise latent S-identification
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\iff\forall\sigma\ \forall x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\ \forall M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma),\ P_{M_0,\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\sigma}^S\Longrightarrow\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_0)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_1)\), where \(\sigma\) ranges over all finite signatures with at least two states for each substantive variable and binary \(S\). Models are compared only within one signature, and every quantified model has declared parent sets and shared-exogenous incidences inducing exactly \(G^S\).

definitions.name: selected S-component kernel
definitions.construction: For a finite signature \(\sigma\) and \(H\subseteq N_S\), \(Q_{P_\sigma}^S[H]=(P_\sigma^S)_{N_S\setminus H}(H\mid A_S,S=1)\). The object \(Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[H]\) denotes this kernel, and every kernel obtained from it by the published topological decomposition and recursive S-component marginalization, evaluated at the coordinates \(X_N=x_N\); all nonintervened arguments retain their displayed or summed values in \(\sigma\).

definitions.name: published Eq. 23 functional
definitions.construction: For every finite signature \(\sigma\) and every outcome value \(y=(y_S,y_N)\in\prod_{v\in Y}\mathcal X_v\), Eq. 23 is the pointwise functional \[\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_\sigma^S)(y)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal X_W} P_\sigma^S(Y_S=y_S,W=w\mid X_S=x_S)\sum_{d_{D\setminus Y_N}\in\mathcal X_{D\setminus Y_N}}\prod_{D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)}Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[D_i]\bigl(d_i\mid y_S,w,x_S,d_{D\setminus D_i}\bigr).\] Every factor is produced by a successful single-component recursion and, at every recursion level, is evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\); the outer conditional is evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\).

definitions.name: selection-ancestor suppression projection
definitions.construction: For the exact augmented graph \(G^S\) induced by the SCM parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences, \(\Pi_S(G^S)\) has vertex set \(N_S\), inherits every directed edge of \(G^S[N_S]\), and has \(u\leftrightarrow v\) exactly when \(G^S\) contains a bidirected path from \(u\) to \(v\) whose internal vertices all lie in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\).

definitions.name: projected ordinary-hedge input record
definitions.construction: For a terminal Algorithm 1 failure at \((C,T)\), \(\mathsf{ProjHedgeInput}(G^S;X,Y;C,T)\) is the set of records \((F_0,F_1,R,\overline M_0,\overline M_1,x_{\mathrm{bin}})\) satisfying all of the following conditions. The graphs \(F_0\subset F_1\subseteq\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) are nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests with vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\), respectively, each has one bidirected district, and exactly the vertices in the nonempty set \(R\subseteq C\) have no children. The Shpitser--Pearl incidence conditions for the originating query hold: \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). The value \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) fixes \(x_N=x_{\mathrm{bin}}|_{X_N}\). The models \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) are finite-binary semi-Markovian SCMs on the projected graph with finite rational latent tables; they induce the same strictly positive projected observational kernel on \(T\), and their named local intervention kernels for the failed factor \(D_i=C\) satisfy \(\overline Q^{(0)}_{C,x_N}\ne\overline Q^{(1)}_{C,x_N}\).

definitions.name: joint fiber-coupling inverse-lift handle
definitions.construction: For a terminal call descended from \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_{\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\) on the exact induced graph \(G^S\), with \(C=D_i\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\) and \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) takes a record \((F_0,F_1,R,\overline M_0,\overline M_1,x_{\mathrm{bin}})\in\mathsf{ProjHedgeInput}(G^S;X,Y;C,T)\). It collects in one incidence hypergraph every original bidirected path through \(A_S\cup\{S\}\) that realizes an edge of \(F_1\), introduces jointly rational parameters of mutually independent finite latent factors that may each enter several endogenous mechanisms and all ancestor mechanisms, imposes equality of every binary-signature selected atom before normalization together with preservation of the common projected observational kernel and the nonzero contrast \(\overline Q^{(0)}_{C,x_N}-\overline Q^{(1)}_{C,x_N}\), eliminates shared or branching ancestor mechanisms in a topological order, and searches the remaining rational nullspace for a lift retaining that local contrast. It then applies \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}\) to complete every declared parent interface and bidirected latent incidence. Its target object is an effective inverse-lift constructor producing \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), with accepted exact checker evidence and realized models whose induced graph equals \(G^S\).

definitions.name: S-Hedge countermodel certificate
definitions.construction: For a terminal Algorithm 1 trace on the exact induced graph \(G^S\), rooted at \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), with initial enclosure \(T_i^{(0)}\), fixed target \(C=D_i\), terminal enclosure \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), and \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), \(\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})=(E_0,E_1)\) is the exact rational pair in \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\) obtained by constructing \((F_0,F_1,R,\overline M_0,\overline M_1,x_{\mathrm{bin}})\in\mathsf{ProjHedgeInput}(G^S;X,Y;C,T)\), applying the effective joint fiber-coupling inverse lift to that record, extending its surviving local \(D_i=C\) contrast through every outside district, and applying \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}\). The returned object includes evidence that both realizations induce exactly \(G^S\) and that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\).

definitions.name: initial-call family and size-sum budget
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_0=\{(D_i,T_i^{(0)}):D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D),\ T_i^{(0)}\in\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S),\ D_i\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\}\), where \(T_i^{(0)}\) is the unique S-component of \(N_S\) containing \(D_i\), and \(B_0=\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|\).

definitions.name: initial d-separation failure certificate
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})=(E_0,E_1)\) applies the positive rational binary countermodel construction from the complete fully observed S-ID necessity proof on \(A_S\cup\{S\}\), extends the same rational mechanisms to every nonancestor vertex, records the result as a pair in \(\operatorname{RawCertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), and applies \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}\) to both members. The returned certificates have every declared parent interface and shared-latent incidence required for their induced graph to equal \(G^S\), and include evidence that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\).

definitions.name: multiset recursion rank
definitions.construction: For the call chains rooted at \(\mathcal I_0\), let \(T_i^{(r)}\) be the current enclosure on root \(i\), with fixed target \(C=D_i\). The rank is \(\rho=\{\!\{|T_i^{(r)}|:i\text{ active}\}\!\}\), ordered by the well-founded multiset extension of \(<\) on \(\mathbb N\). A recursive step replaces \(T_i^{(r)}\) by the S-component \(T_i^{(r+1)}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T_i^{(r)}]}(D_i)\subsetneq T_i^{(r)}\) containing \(D_i\).

definitions.name: executable S-ID success-or-certificate algorithm
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) runs published Algorithm 1 on a finite augmented ADMG \(G^S\) with childless \(S\), interpreted as the exact graph induced by the SCM parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences, and records \(\mathcal I_0\). Given any finite signature \(\sigma\), on success at intervention value \(x\in\mathcal X_X\) it returns \(\operatorname{ID}(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma})\). If the initial d-separation check fails it chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) and returns \(\operatorname{NONID}(x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1,\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), where \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) and both certificates induce exactly \(G^S\). If the call rooted at \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\) reaches a terminal failure \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(C,T,Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T])\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), both \(C\) and \(T\) are single S-components, and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\); the algorithm chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and returns the same encoded \(\operatorname{NONID}\) object with \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). This total failure branch is enabled only by a proved effective inverse-lift constructor returning rational exact-graph \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) objects; an existential arbitrary-SCM lift does not implement \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\). The trace stores the multiset rank before and after every recursive call.

definitions.name: two-virtual-edge early-kill instance
definitions.construction: On \(V_\star=\{B,D,Y,Z_1,Z_2\}\), set \(X_\star=\{B,D\}\), \(Y_\star=\{Y\}\), and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star}=(\{0,1\})_{v\in V_\star\cup\{S\}}\). For \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\), the early-kill calculation eliminates exact rational response-type parameters over \(E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1}\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\), with \(M_{\star,i}=\llbracket E_{\star,i}\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_{\star,+}\), subject to exact induced-graph equality with \(G_\star^S\), \(P_{M_{\star,0}}(V_\star=v\mid S=1)=P_{M_{\star,1}}(V_\star=v\mid S=1)>0\) for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^{V_\star}\), and \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(M_{\star,0})\ne Q_{\star,x_\star}(M_{\star,1})\). A separating pair must also satisfy the local instance of \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept}\), including exact parent-interface and shared-latent incidence validation. The local instance is embedded in the generic notation by substituting \(V_\star,G_\star^S,X_\star,Y_\star,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star},x_\star,E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1},M_{\star,0},M_{\star,1}\) for \(V,G^S,X,Y,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}},x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1,M_0,M_1\), respectively.

definitions.name: positive exact-graph two-selector augmented-SCM class
definitions.construction: For every finite two-selector signature \(\sigma_{EI}\), \(\mathfrak M_{EI,+}(G^{EI},\sigma_{EI})=\{M_{EI}:M_{EI}\text{ is recursive with mutually independent exogenous variables, }S_E\text{ and }S_I\text{ are childless, }\operatorname{Pa}_{M_{EI}}(v)=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^{EI}}(v)\text{ for every }v,\ v\leftrightarrow w\in G^{EI}\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal U_{M_{EI}}^v\cap\mathcal U_{M_{EI}}^w\ne\varnothing\text{ for every distinct }v,w,\text{ and }P_{M_{EI}}(V_{EI}=z,S_r=1)>0\text{ for every }z\text{ and }r\in\{E,I\}\}\).

definitions.name: Tian exposure--imaging observation map
definitions.construction: For \(M_{EI}\in\mathfrak M_{EI,+}(G^{EI},\sigma_{EI})\), \(\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI})=(P_{M_{EI}}(Z,A,L\mid S_E=1),P_{M_{EI}}(Z,Y,L\mid S_I=1))\). The two selectors and the two observed margins remain distinct.

definitions.name: Tian exact-graph feasibility fiber
definitions.construction: For an observed pair \(\mathcal O\), \(\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})=\{M_{EI}\in\mathfrak M_{EI,+}(G^{EI},\sigma_{EI}):\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI})=\mathcal O\}\).

definitions.name: imaging-selected full-law set induced by the feasibility fiber
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma_I(\mathcal O;G^{EI})=\{P_{M_{EI}}(V_{EI}\mid S_I=1):M_{EI}\in\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\}\).

definitions.name: conditional UK Biobank feasibility audit
definitions.construction: Given \(\mathcal O,G^{EI},\sigma_{EI},a\), \(\mathsf{Audit}_{EI}\) first tests whether \(\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\) is nonempty and records \(\Gamma_I(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\). It returns a data-compatible nonidentification record displaying \(M_{EI,0},M_{EI,1}\) only with two displayed models in that same fiber satisfying \(\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,0})\ne\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,1})\). Without such a pair it returns only an unmet-assumptions report listing the additional fusion or selected-instrument assumptions needed to reduce the fiber, or an inconclusive result.

definitions.name: native actual-incidence terminal trace
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds when: (i) \(G^S\) is a finite acyclic directed mixed graph on \(V\cup\{S\}\), \(S\) has no children, \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\), and \(Y\ne\varnothing\); (ii) the initial selected d-separation check of published Algorithm 1 passes; and (iii) for every \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\) and every reachable terminal failed call \((C,T)\) on the chain rooted at the unique \(T_i^{(0)}\in\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), one has \(C=D_i\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), both \(G^S[C]\) and \(G^S[T]\) are bidirected-connected, and there exist \(R=C\) and nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) with vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\), respectively, such that every directed and bidirected edge of both forests is an actual edge of \(G^S[N_S]\), \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). Compatibility on such an input remains the exact induced-graph compatibility of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\); the predicate restricts graph traces, not mechanisms on a fixed graph.

definitions.name: finite-signature inert exact-graph completion
definitions.construction: Let \(\widetilde M\) be a recursive augmented SCM with finite endogenous signature \(\widetilde\sigma\) on \(V\cup\{S\}\), whose declared parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce an augmented ADMG contained in \(G^S\). The completion \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}(\widetilde M)\) adds each missing parent in \(\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) to the declared interface of \(v\) and makes the structural function constant in that coordinate. For every listed bidirected edge not already witnessed by shared exogenous incidence, it adds a fresh independent nondegenerate finite latent factor incident to its endpoints and makes both structural functions constant in that factor. It introduces no other interface or shared incidence and leaves all original state spaces, exogenous laws, and structural values unchanged.

statements.statement: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\), and every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), strict selected-cell positivity on \(\prod_{v\in V}\mathcal X_v\) and SCM consistency imply \(P_M(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))>0\). Hence \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) is defined without an additional postintervention support assumption.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\sigma\), \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\), and \(x\in\mathcal X_X\).  Because every substantive state space is nonempty, choose \(z\in\mathcal X_{V\setminus X}\), and put \(v=(x,z)\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}cell\text{-}positivity}\),
\[
  P_M(V=v,S=1)>0. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(U\) denote the complete exogenous input and let
\[
  A_v=\{u:V_M(u)=v,\ S_M(u)=1\}.
\]
Equation (1) says \(P_U(A_v)>0\).  We claim that every \(u\in A_v\) also gives \(S=1\) after \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\).  Indeed, order the endogenous vertices topologically, which is possible by the recursiveness clause of \(\mathrm{ass:augmented\text{-}scm\text{-}compatibility}\).  At a vertex in \(X\), the intervention assigns the value \(x\), which is its already realized value on \(A_v\).  At a vertex outside \(X\), if all preceding parents retain their observational values, its unchanged structural function, evaluated at the same exogenous input, retains its observational value.  Induction over the topological order therefore leaves every nonintervened endogenous variable, in particular \(S\), unchanged.  Thus
\[
  A_v\subseteq\{u:S_{M,x}(u)=1\}.
\]
The intervention does not alter the law of \(U\), so
\[
  P_M(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
  =P_U\{S_{M,x}(U)=1\}
  \ge P_U(A_v)>0. \tag{2}
\]
The denominator in the intervention-before-conditioning definition of \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) is therefore positive by (2), proving the claim.
statements.justification: This removes a redundant support premise while keeping intervention-before-conditioning mathematically defined.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID assumes a strictly positive selected observational law but does not isolate this consistency consequence as a separate lemma.
statements.consumer: Every graphwise comparison and every finite-binary failure certificate can use the selected intervention target without strengthening the published model class.

statements.statement: For every finite binary table encoding \(E\in\operatorname{RawCertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}(E)\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). Its realized SCM has declared observed-parent set exactly \(\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) at every \(v\), and two distinct mechanisms share an exogenous input if and only if their vertices are joined by a bidirected edge in \(G^S\). Moreover, \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\) and \(\llbracket\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}(E)\rrbracket\) induce the same observational law on \(V\cup\{S\}\), the same postintervention law under \(\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}})\), and \(\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E\rrbracket)=\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}(E)\rrbracket)\).
statements.justification: The published graph is induced syntactically by declared parent sets and shared exogenous inputs, so every certificate must meet graph equality rather than adjacency containment.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID defines exact graph induction but does not give a finite-certificate exactification lemma preserving selected observational and interventional laws.
statements.consumer: Ordinary hedge and fully observed necessity witnesses can be embedded into the exact published augmented graph without changing their observable equality or target separation.

statements.statement: Every encoding \(E\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) realizes a recursive augmented SCM \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). Its finite latent factors are mutually independent by their product law, a factor may feed any number of mechanisms, every declared parent set equals the corresponding parent set in \(G^S\), shared exogenous incidence induces exactly the bidirected edges of \(G^S\), and every selected atom is positive. Hence \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\subseteq\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) under the realization map, without restricting the ambient graphwise identification quantifier.
statements.proof_tex:
Take \(E\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).  Its directed structural tables can be evaluated in a topological order because the directed part of \(G^S\) is acyclic.  Thus their interpretation \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\) is a recursive augmented SCM.  By \(\mathrm{def:certscm\text{-}encoding}\), the joint latent mass is
\[
  p(u_1,\ldots,u_m)=\prod_{j=1}^m p_j(u_j),
\]
so the latent factors are mutually independent; the definition imposes no two-mechanism restriction on a scope \(I_j\).  The same definition gives, for every endogenous vertex \(v\),
\[
  P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v), \tag{5}
\]
and, for every pair of distinct vertices \(v,w\),
\[
 v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists j\;\{v,w\}\subseteq I_j. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5) and (6) are exactly the parent-interface and shared-exogenous clauses of \(\mathrm{ass:augmented\text{-}scm\text{-}compatibility}\).  Finally, membership in the certificate type requires
\[
 P_{\llbracket E\rrbracket}(V=z,S=1)>0
 \quad\text{for every }z\in\{0,1\}^{V}, \tag{7}
\]
which is \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}cell\text{-}positivity}\) for the binary signature.  Recursiveness, (5), (6), and (7) are precisely the membership clauses of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).  Hence \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).
statements.justification: This separates a finitely checkable witness language from the unrestricted model class over which identification is defined.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID permits shared exogenous variables but does not define a finite exact syntax for countermodels or prove its interpretation compatible with that class.
statements.consumer: Every accepted encoded NONID object becomes a valid counterexample to graphwise identification in the exact induced-graph class of AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID.

statements.statement: For \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), if \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\), then the realized models lie in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), satisfy \(P_{\llbracket E_0\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}^S=P_{\llbracket E_1\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}^S>0\) on every binary cell, and satisfy \(\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_0\rrbracket)\ne\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_1\rrbracket)\). The checker terminates after at most \(c\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations for a universal implementation constant \(c\).
statements.proof_tex:
Assume that the checker accepts \((E_0,E_1)\).  Its initial validation, by \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\), verifies the complete rational latent tables, their product-factor interpretation, all structural tables, and exact equality of the induced graph with \(G^S\).  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:certscm\text{-}ambient\text{-}inclusion}\) gives
\[
  \llbracket E_i\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}),
  \qquad i=0,1. \tag{8}
\]
For a binary substantive atom \(v\), let
\[
 a_i(v)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1),
 \qquad z_i=\sum_v a_i(v).
\]
Acceptance requires \(a_i(v)>0\) for every \(v\).  Hence \(z_i>0\), and it also requires
\[
 a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\qquad\text{for every }v. \tag{9}
\]
Dividing (9) by the positive number \(z_0z_1\) yields
\[
 P^S_{\llbracket E_0\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(v)
 =\frac{a_0(v)}{z_0}
 =\frac{a_1(v)}{z_1}
 =P^S_{\llbracket E_1\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(v)>0. \tag{10}
\]
After replacing the tables at \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the checker computes
\[
 b_i(y)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}
   (Y=y,S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}})),
 \qquad q_i=\sum_y b_i(y).
\]
Acceptance requires \(q_0q_1>0\) and, for some \(y\),
\[
 b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0. \tag{11}
\]
Thus both intervention-before-conditioning distributions are defined, and division of (11) by \(q_0q_1\) gives
\[
 \Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_0\rrbracket)(y)
 =\frac{b_0(y)}{q_0}
 \ne\frac{b_1(y)}{q_1}
 =\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_1\rrbracket)(y). \tag{12}
\]

It remains to justify the stated operation bound.  Table and normalization validation costs at most a constant multiple of \(L(E_0)+L(E_1)\); checking all vertex pairs costs \(O(|V|^2)\).  For model \(i\), each observational or postintervention pass enumerates \(R(E_i)\) latent assignments, evaluates at most \(|V|+1\) endogenous tables in topological order, and updates an atom table.  Inspecting all substantive atoms costs \(O(2^{|V|})\), and inspecting all outcome atoms costs \(O(2^{|Y|})\le O(2^{|V|})\).  Since \(R(E_i)\ge1\), all these terms are bounded, after increasing one universal implementation constant \(c\), by
\[
 c\left\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)
 +2^{|V|}\bigl(R(E_0)+R(E_1)\bigr)(|V|+|Y|+1)\right\}.
\]
Every loop has a finite explicitly encoded range, so the checker terminates.  Equations (8), (10), and (12) prove its semantic soundness.
statements.justification: The failure branch is reproducible only when finite syntax, exact equality, target separation, and an explicit enumeration bound are certified together.
statements.gap: Neither latent S-ID nor ordinary hedge completeness supplies an exact certificate checker for normalized selected-law equality under shared exogenous incidence.
statements.consumer: Independent software can validate a returned failure witness without trusting the inverse-lift implementation.

statements.statement: Let \(G^S\) be the exact augmented graph induced by any \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\). For every \(H\subseteq N_S\), the districts of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\) are exactly \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\). More precisely, two vertices of \(H\) are bidirected-connected in \(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]\) if and only if they are bidirected-connected in \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(H\subseteq N_S\).  Suppose first that \(u,v\in H\) are joined by a bidirected path \(\gamma\) in \(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]\).  List, in their order along \(\gamma\), the vertices of \(\gamma\) that lie in \(H\):
\[
  h_0=u,h_1,\ldots,h_r=v.
\]
The internal vertices of the subpath from \(h_{j-1}\) to \(h_j\) lie outside \(H\), and every vertex of \(\gamma\) lies in \(H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Since \(H\subseteq N_S\) and \(A_S\cap N_S=\varnothing\), those internal vertices lie in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:suppression\text{-}projection}\), \(h_{j-1}\leftrightarrow h_j\) is therefore an edge of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).  Hence \(u\) and \(v\) are bidirected-connected in the projection.

Conversely, suppose \(u=h_0,\ldots,h_r=v\) is a bidirected path in \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).  For each projected edge \(h_{j-1}\leftrightarrow h_j\), \(\mathrm{def:suppression\text{-}projection}\) supplies a bidirected path in \(G^S\) whose internal vertices lie in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Concatenating these finitely many paths gives a bidirected walk from \(u\) to \(v\) contained in \(H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Deleting closed subwalks gives a bidirected path in the same induced graph.  Thus the two bidirected-connectivity relations on \(H\) coincide.  Districts are the equivalence classes of bidirected connectivity, while \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\) is defined in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}component}\) by intersecting the original districts with \(H\).  The asserted equality of partitions follows.
statements.justification: This establishes that S-components are ordinary districts after the precise suppression operation.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID defines S-components through ancestors of selection but does not state this projection equivalence.
statements.consumer: The ordinary hedge countermodel theorem of ShpitserPearl2006 can be invoked only after this graph-level correspondence is certified.

statements.statement: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), so \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\). Moreover, \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) are single districts, \(\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)=T\), and there are nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) in the projection, with \(R=C\), vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\), and \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) also holds, the forests can instead be chosen as subgraphs of \(G^S[N_S]\), so every directed and bidirected forest edge is an actual edge of the original nonancestor graph and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). These are graph-theoretic conclusions only; they assert no binary, rational, or positive countermodel construction.
statements.proof_tex:
The target of every call on the chain is fixed at \(C=D_i\) by \(\mathrm{def:success\text{-}or\text{-}certificate\text{-}algorithm}\). At a terminal failure,
\[
 C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\},\qquad
 \operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
These are exactly the clauses of \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:projection\text{-}components}\) with \(H=C\) and \(H=T\). The two singleton S-component identities imply that \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) each have one district. Projection preserves all and only directed edges with endpoints in \(N_S\), so
\[
 \operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)
 =\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
Choose a bidirected spanning tree \(K_0\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\). Starting from \(K_0\), repeatedly attach a vertex outside the current set by the first edge on a bidirected path to that set; this gives a spanning tree \(K_1\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) with \(K_1[C]=K_0\). Put \(R=C\). Give \(F_0\) vertex set \(C\), bidirected tree \(K_0\), and no directed edges. For \(t\in T\setminus C\), define
\[
 d(t)=\min\{\ell:\text{a directed path of length }\ell
 \text{ runs from }t\text{ to }C\text{ in }G^S[T]\}.
\]
The ancestral equality makes \(d(t)\) finite. Choose a next vertex \(c(t)\) on a shortest path and put \(t\to c(t)\) in \(F_1\). Since \(d(c(t))=d(t)-1\), there is no directed cycle; vertices outside \(C\) have one child and vertices in \(C\) have none. With bidirected tree \(K_1\), \(F_1\) is an \(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forest and \(F_1[C]=F_0\).

From \(D=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) and \(C=D_i\subseteq D\),
\[
 C\cap X_N=\varnothing,\qquad
 R=C\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)
 =\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).
\]
If \(T\cap X_N=\varnothing\), every \(t\in T\) reaches \(C\), and every vertex of \(C\) reaches \(Y_N\), inside \(N_S\setminus X_N\). Thus \(T\subseteq D\). Since \(T\) is one S-component containing the S-component \(D_i=C\) of \(D\), maximality of \(D_i\) gives \(T\subseteq C\), contrary to \(C\subsetneq T\). Hence \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\).

If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, its terminal-trace clause supplies forests with the same vertex, root, and incidence properties whose edges all belong to \(G^S[N_S]\). This proves the native conclusion. No step constructs a causal model.
statements.justification: This proves terminal S-Hedge geometry and projected/native forest extraction only.
statements.gap: Countermodels require separate positive finite constructions.
statements.consumer: Both the native separator and universal inverse-lift OEQ use the forest skeleton.

statements.statement:
Fix an actual terminal call for \(D_i=C\) and two candidate full-graph extensions that use kernels \(q_C^{(0)}\) and \(q_C^{(1)}\) in the \(C\)-position, the same kernels \(q_j\) for every \(D_j\ne C\), and the same outer selected conditional \(p^S\). Their pointwise Eq. 23 product contrast is
\[
 \Delta(y)=\sum_{w,d_{D\setminus Y_N}}
 p^S(y_S,w\mid x_S)
 \bigl(q_C^{(0)}-q_C^{(1)}\bigr)
 \prod_{D_j\ne C}q_j.
\]
The two constructed full targets differ if and only if \(\Delta(y)\ne0\) for at least one outcome value \(y\). Strict positivity of \(p^S\) and of the common factors, together with \(q_C^{(0)}\ne q_C^{(1)}\), does not by itself imply this nonvanishing condition.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), substitute \(q_C^{(r)}\), the common \(q_j\) for \(D_j\ne C\), and the common \(p^S\) into \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\). Finiteness permits termwise subtraction, and distributivity gives
\[
 \Phi^{(0)}(y)-\Phi^{(1)}(y)
 =\sum_{w,d_{D\setminus Y_N}}
 p^S(y_S,w\mid x_S)
 \bigl(q_C^{(0)}-q_C^{(1)}\bigr)
 \prod_{D_j\ne C}q_j
 =\Delta(y).
\]
Two measures on finite \(Y\) are unequal exactly when one point mass is unequal, proving the equivalence.

Positivity does not make this contraction injective. For binary \((A,R)\), take
\[
 q_C^{(0)}(0,0)=q_C^{(0)}(1,1)=\frac38,\quad
 q_C^{(0)}(1,0)=q_C^{(0)}(0,1)=\frac18,\quad
 q_C^{(1)}(a,r)=\frac14.
\]
Both kernels are positive and unequal, but for each \(r\),
\[
 \sum_a\bigl(q_C^{(0)}(a,r)-q_C^{(1)}(a,r)\bigr)=0.
\]
If \(A\subseteq D\setminus Y_N\) is marginalized and all common factors are independent of \(A\), the contraction contains this zero sum, so \(\Delta(y)=0\) for every \(y\). This is the claimed obstruction.
statements.justification: This gives the exact contraction test and an explicit positive cancellation witness.
statements.gap: Local inequality alone does not imply target inequality.
statements.consumer: Any future universal extension must certify a nonzero outcome contrast.

statements.statement: Can the joint fiber-coupling handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) be completed as an effective exact-rational constructor for every terminal Algorithm 1 S-Hedge whose projected forest uses virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching vertices of \(A_S\cup\{S\}\)? It must output \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), preserve one common strictly positive normalized selected law, and certify a named nonzero event contrast in \(\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}\), not merely an unequal local kernel. It must jointly realize all virtual edges, terminate with finite rational tables, induce exactly \(G^S\), and use \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}\) only through \(\mathrm{lem:exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\). The positive-binary two-virtual-edge instance is separately unresolved; only a support-deficient separator and two no-go subclasses are established.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a terminal call \((C,T)\). By \(\mathrm{lem:shedge\text{-}projects\text{-}to\text{-}hedge}\), the suppression graph supplies nested ordinary hedge forests in \(\Pi_S(G^S)\). This conclusion is purely graph-theoretic: when a forest edge \(u\leftrightarrow v\) is virtual, it gives only a bidirected path from \(u\) to \(v\) with internal vertices in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\), not a compatible structural realization of the projected shared latent.

There is nevertheless a complete computable reduction of the remaining task. For a proposed certificate \(E_j\), let \(\mathcal U_j\) be its finite joint latent support, let
\[
 \lambda_j(u)=\prod_{\ell=1}^{m(E_j)}p_{j\ell}(u_\ell),
\]
and let \(F_j(u)\) and \(F^{x}_{j}(u)\) be, respectively, the deterministic observed vector before intervention and after replacing the equations for \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\). Define
\[
 a_j(v)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_j}\lambda_j(u)
 \mathbf 1\{F_j(u)|_V=v,\ F_j(u)|_S=1\},
 \qquad z_j=\sum_v a_j(v),
\]
and
\[
 b_j(y)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_j}\lambda_j(u)
 \mathbf 1\{F^x_j(u)|_Y=y,\ F^x_j(u)|_S=1\},
 \qquad q_j=\sum_y b_j(y).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\), after its syntax and exact-incidence tests the checker accepts exactly when
\[
 a_j(v)>0\quad(j=0,1;\ v\in\{0,1\}^V),
 \qquad a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\quad(v\in\{0,1\}^V),
\]
\[
 q_0q_1>0,
 \qquad b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0
 \quad\hbox{for some }y\in\{0,1\}^Y.
\]
The first line is precisely strict selected-cell positivity and equality of the two normalized selected laws, because \(z_0,z_1>0\). The second line is precisely a named atomic-event contrast between the intervention-before-conditioning targets. These are exactly the checker-visible constraints. The inverse-lift handle must additionally impose the finite rational equalities that identify the appropriate restrictions of these tables with the common projected observational kernel and the two carried local kernels \(\overline Q^{(j)}_{C,x_N}\). Thus the desired inverse lift is equivalent to producing finite rational tables satisfying the displayed constraints, those record-preservation equalities, and the original latent-scope and parent-interface restrictions. Once a raw pair satisfies them, \(\mathrm{lem:exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\) permits completion of missing allowed incidences without changing any displayed quantity.

For fixed \((G^S,X,Y)\), existence of such a rational certificate is semidecidable. Enumerate \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and all pairs of finite rational table strings in increasing total encoded length, and run \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}\) on each pair. Every individual run terminates by the explicit operation bound in \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\), and the enumeration reaches every member of \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\). Hence it halts with an accepted pair if and only if such a pair exists. What is missing is the mathematical existence theorem, not a checker or a search procedure conditional on existence.

The frozen results do not provide that existence theorem. In particular, \(\overline Q^{(0)}_{C,x_N}\ne\overline Q^{(1)}_{C,x_N}\) cannot replace the final inequality above: by \(\mathrm{lem:local\text{-}contrast\text{-}survives\text{-}eq23}\), summation over \(w\) and \(D\setminus Y_N\) can cancel the local contrast. Independent construction along each suppressed path also does not compose at a shared or branching internal ancestor, because the same observed mechanism then occurs in several path constraints while the exogenous factors must remain mutually independent. The smallest unresolved specialization is \(G_\star^S\): a universal constructor would in particular produce the accepted positive binary pair asked for by \(\mathrm{oeq:positive\text{-}binary\text{-}two\text{-}virtual\text{-}edge\text{-}separation}\). The available support-deficient pair fails the inequalities \(a_j(v)>0\), while \(\mathrm{lem:independent\text{-}smoothing\text{-}kills\text{-}early\text{-}contrast}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:affine\text{-}fair\text{-}bit\text{-}early\text{-}target\text{-}half}\) exclude only two restricted response families. Therefore neither a positive universal construction nor a negative impossibility certificate follows from the frozen core.
statements.justification: This retains the genuinely virtual-edge realization problem as open.
statements.gap: No positive rational common-selected-law construction is known for shared or branching ancestor paths.
statements.consumer: Universal completeness and total terminal compilation require it.

statements.statement:
For every finite augmented ADMG \(G^S\) with childless \(S\), whenever published Algorithm 1 reaches its single-component recursion, every call chain terminates. Its chain rooted at \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, the recursion depth is at most \(\max_i|T_i^{(0)}|\le|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most \(B_0\). Independently, for any supplied \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), the exact NONID checker terminates within
\[
 c\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}
\]
exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations. If it accepts, the realized models induce exactly \(G^S\), have the same strictly positive selected law, and have unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. This theorem proves graph-recursion termination and certificate-verification soundness only; it does not assert that either failure branch can always compile such a certificate or that \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) is total.
statements.proof_tex: The recursion assertions are \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\). For supplied \(E_0,E_1\), \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\) exhaustively enumerates finite latent, observational, and outcome cells and has the displayed operation bound. By \(\mathrm{lem:certificate\text{-}checker\text{-}soundness}\), acceptance places both realizations in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), proves equality and positivity of their selected laws, and proves target inequality at \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\). Neither premise constructs a certificate, so no totality conclusion follows.
statements.justification: This proves recursion and supplied-certificate checking bounds without false totality.
statements.gap: The checker verifies but does not generate certificates.
statements.consumer: Implementations obtain certified finite control flow and verification cost.

statements.statement: Known-case regression corollary. If \(G^S\) has no bidirected edges and \(S\) has no children, then for every \(H\subseteq N_S\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\) is the singleton partition of \(H\), and no recursive S-Hedge exists. Consequently the recursive S-Hedge failure branch of \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) cannot occur. The latent-paper criterion reduces to its initial selected d-separation condition, which the published paper states is consistent with the fully observed S-ID criterion. Whenever the latent Algorithm 1 succeeds, its returned \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}\) identifies \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}\) by published soundness. This corollary does not assert byte-for-byte equality of the two papers' displayed formulas.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume that \(G^S\) has no bidirected edges and that \(S\) has no children.  Fix \(H\subseteq N_S\), and write
\[
  J_H=G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}].
\]
Taking an induced subgraph cannot create an edge, so \(J_H\) has no bidirected edges.  A district is a maximal set joined by bidirected paths.  A bidirected path between two distinct vertices contains a bidirected edge; hence every district of \(J_H\) is a singleton.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}component}\) therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)
 &=\bigl\{K\cap H:K\in\mathcal D(J_H),\ K\cap H\ne\varnothing\bigr\}\\
 &=\bigl\{\{h\}:h\in H\bigr\}. \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
When \(H=\varnothing\), both sides of (1) are the empty partition, so (1) covers every \(H\subseteq N_S\).

We next exclude an S-Hedge directly from the definitions.  Suppose for contradiction that \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) holds.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\),
\[
 C\subsetneq T\subseteq N_S,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}. \tag{2}
\]
The declared type of \(C\) makes \(C\) nonempty, so choose \(t\in C\).  Since \(t\in T\), (1) applied with \(H=T\) says that \(\{t\}\) is a block of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)\).  Combining this fact with (2) yields \(\{t\}=T\).  The inclusions \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq T=\{t\}\) then force \(C=T\), contradicting \(C\subsetneq T\).  Thus
\[
  \neg\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)
  \quad\text{for every admissible pair }(C,T). \tag{3}
\]

Definition \(\mathrm{def:success\text{-}or\text{-}certificate\text{-}algorithm}\) states that a terminal recursive failure supplies sets \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq N_S\) such that both are single S-components and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\), those conditions are exactly \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\).  This contradicts (3), so the recursive S-Hedge failure branch of \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) cannot occur.  This argument proves the singleton-component and no-failure conclusions internally; it does not borrow them from the citation.

For the remaining graphical comparison, \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}dag\text{-}sid\text{-}consistency}\) records the precise DAG specialization of AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID Theorem 5.1 and the paragraph immediately following Remark 5.2: the auxiliary effect is always s-ID, while the original selected causal effect is s-ID exactly when the paper's Equation (5), its initial selected d-separation condition, holds; the authors call this consistent with AboueiEtAl2024SID Theorem 2.  This is a comparison of graphical criteria and does not assert literal equality of the two papers' displayed formulas.

It remains to verify the identifying claim as an equality between the observed-law functional and the causal target.  Fix a finite signature \(\sigma\), an intervention value \(x\in\mathcal X_X\), and a model \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:target\text{-}support}\),
\[
  P_M\bigl(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x)\bigr)>0, \tag{4}
\]
so the intervention-before-conditioning law \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) is defined.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\),
\[
  P_M(V=v,S=1)>0
  \quad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j. \tag{5}
\]
Summing (5) over the nonempty finite state space of \(V\) gives \(P_M(S=1)>0\), and hence
\[
  P_{M,\sigma}^S(v)
  =\frac{P_M(V=v,S=1)}{P_M(S=1)}>0. \tag{6}
\]
More generally, for any \(Z\subseteq V\) and \(z\in\mathcal X_Z\), finiteness of the signature and (6) give
\[
  P_{M,\sigma}^S(Z=z)
  =\sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V:\,v|_Z=z}P_{M,\sigma}^S(v)>0, \tag{7}
\]
because the set of completions of \(z\) is nonempty and every summand is positive.  Thus every observed-coordinate conditioning denominator used in the outer conditional and in the successful finite recursive selected-kernel construction is positive.

Now suppose published Algorithm 1 succeeds.  Its soundness theorem, recorded as \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}latent\text{-}sid\text{-}soundness}\), applies because of (4)--(7).  Using Definition \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\), it yields, for every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)(y)
 =P_M\bigl(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),S=1\bigr)
 =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)(y). \tag{8}
\]
Since \(\mathcal X_Y\) is finite, the pointwise equalities in (8) imply equality of probability laws.

Finally, let \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) have the same selected observational law \(P_{M_0,\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\sigma}^S=p\).  Applying (8) to each model gives
\[
  \Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_0)
  =\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(p)
  =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_1). \tag{9}
\]
Therefore the explicit observed-law map \(p\mapsto\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(p)\) identifies \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}\) whenever Algorithm 1 succeeds, as claimed.
statements.justification: The narrowed corollary matches the exact published comparison.
statements.gap: Literal term-by-term equality of the two papers' formulas was not sourced or derived.
statements.consumer: The DAG case remains a graphical and semantic regression test.

statements.statement: Fix a finite two-selector signature \(\sigma_{EI}\), an exact induced graph \(G^{EI}\), an observed pair \(\mathcal O=(P(Z,A,L\mid S_E=1),P(Z,Y,L\mid S_I=1))\), and \(a\in\mathcal X_A\). If \(\mathsf{Audit}_{EI}\) exhibits \(M_{EI,0},M_{EI,1}\in\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\) with \(\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,0})\ne\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,1})\), then the imaging-selected HbA1c intervention target is not identified from those two observed Tian margins over the positive exact-graph two-selector class. Such membership establishes that the fiber is nonempty and that both models have exactly the declared parent interfaces and shared-latent incidences. The audit may return a UK Biobank data-compatible nonidentification conclusion only with this same-fiber pair. Otherwise it returns only unmet fusion or selected-instrument assumptions, or an inconclusive result. In particular, a generic one-selector \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair with one common full selected law is not a certificate for the two Tian margins unless both realized models are separately verified to belong to the same \(\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\) fiber.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\sigma_{EI}\), \(G^{EI}\), \(\mathcal O\), and \(a\) as in the statement, and abbreviate
\[
 \mathfrak M=\mathfrak M_{EI,+}(G^{EI},\sigma_{EI}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal F=\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI}).
\]
We first verify that every conditional law used below is well defined.  If \(N\in\mathfrak M\), then, by \(\mathrm{ass:exposure\text{-}selector\text{-}positivity}\), \(\mathrm{ass:imaging\text{-}selector\text{-}positivity}\), and \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}selector\text{-}model\text{-}class}\), for each \(r\in\{E,I\}\) and each substantive cell \(v\),
\[
 P_N(V_{EI}=v,S_r=1)>0.
\]
Because the signature is finite and its product state space is nonempty, summation over all substantive cells gives
\[
 P_N(S_r=1)
 =\sum_{v\in\prod_{k\in V_{EI}}\mathcal X_k}
   P_N(V_{EI}=v,S_r=1)>0.
\]
Thus both components of \(\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(N)\), as defined in \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}observation\text{-}map}\), exist.  Moreover,
\[
 P_N(A=a,S_I=1)
 =\sum_{v:v_A=a}P_N(V_{EI}=v,S_I=1)>0.
\]
The model is recursive by \(\mathrm{ass:two\text{-}selector\text{-}exact\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}selector\text{-}model\text{-}class}\).  For any exogenous realization at which the observational solution has \(A=a\), replacing the structural equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) leaves the entire solution unchanged: this follows by induction along a topological ordering, since the replacement agrees with the observational value at \(A\), and every later structural function receives the same parent values and the same exogenous inputs.  Consequently
\[
 \{A=a,S_I=1\}_{\mathrm{obs}}
 \subseteq
 \{S_I=1\}_{\operatorname{do}(A=a)},
\]
and hence
\[
 P_N(S_I=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))
 \ge P_N(A=a,S_I=1)>0.
\]
Therefore \(\Theta^I_a(N)=P_N(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),S_I=1)\), with intervention performed before conditioning as specified by the symbol \(\Theta^I_a\), is also well defined.

We now separate the causal target from the observation map.  Point identification of \(\Theta^I_a\) from the two Tian margins over \(\mathfrak M\) means the following property:
\[
 \mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{for all }N_0,N_1\in\mathfrak M,
 \quad
 \operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(N_0)=\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(N_1)
 \Longrightarrow
 \Theta^I_a(N_0)=\Theta^I_a(N_1).
\]
This line is the definition of identification relative to the stated observation map; it does not define the causal target, which was defined independently by intervention followed by conditioning.

Suppose that the audit exhibits \(M_{EI,0},M_{EI,1}\in\mathcal F\) with
\[
 \Theta^I_a(M_{EI,0})\ne\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,1}).
\]
Unfolding \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}feasibility\text{-}fiber}\) separately for \(j=0,1\) yields
\[
 M_{EI,j}\in\mathfrak M
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI,j})=\mathcal O.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI,0})
 =\mathcal O
 =\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI,1}),
\]
whereas their causal targets differ.  The pair therefore falsifies the universal implication defining \(\mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a)\), so
\[
 \neg\mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a).
\]
This proves nonidentification from the two observed margins over the positive exact-graph two-selector class.

The same membership statements also prove \(\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\).  Furthermore, by \(\mathrm{ass:two\text{-}selector\text{-}exact\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}selector\text{-}model\text{-}class}\), each displayed model has exactly the parent interfaces of \(G^{EI}\), and two distinct endogenous mechanisms share an exogenous input if and only if their vertices are joined by a bidirected edge of \(G^{EI}\).  Thus permitted edges are not being silently deleted or added.  By \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}imaging\text{-}law\text{-}set}\), the full imaging-selected laws compatible with the two margins are exactly
\[
 \Gamma_I(\mathcal O;G^{EI})
 =\{P_N(V_{EI}\mid S_I=1):N\in\mathcal F\},
\]
which is the set recorded by the audit.

Finally, unfold \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}feasibility\text{-}audit}\).  Its nonidentification branch is enabled only by two displayed models in the same fiber whose \(\Theta^I_a\)-values differ.  If no such pair is displayed, that definition permits only an unmet-assumptions report identifying additional fusion or selected-instrument assumptions, or an inconclusive output.  A one-selector \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair with a common law \(P(V\mid S=1)\) does not, merely from that fact, instantiate the two quantifiers in \(\mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a)\): its members have not thereby been shown to lie in \(\mathfrak M\), and equality of one common selected law has not thereby been shown to equal the ordered two-selector observation \(\mathcal O\).  Separate verification that both realized models belong to the same \(\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\) is therefore a necessary condition for that pair to serve as a certificate for the Tian margins.  This proves every asserted branch of the proposition.
