statements.statement: In the following legal raw response family for the early-kill graph, independent smoothing cannot preserve a target contrast. Let \(U,W,Z_1\) be independent fair bits, let \(E\) be an independent bit with \(0<P(E=1)<1\), and use the same strictly positive selection probabilities given \((Z_1,Z_2)\) in two models. Both models set \(B=U\) and \(D=B\oplus E\). Model zero sets \(Z_2=U\oplus W\), model one sets \(Z_2=W\), and model \(j\) uses a Bernoulli outcome kernel \(P_j(Y=1\mid D=d,W=w)=\kappa_j(d,w)\). If their selected observational laws agree, then for each \(d\), \(\kappa_0(d,0)=\kappa_0(d,1)=\kappa_1(d,0)=\kappa_1(d,1)\); consequently their selected targets under \(\operatorname{do}(B=0,D=d)\) are equal. Coordinate-constant exactification cannot change this conclusion.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(U\) and \(W\) are fair and independent, \((B,Z_2)\) is uniform in both models. The variable \(Z_1\), the conditional law of \(D\) given \(B\), and the positive selection kernel are also common. In particular every stratum \((b,d,z_1,z_2,S=1)\) has positive probability because \(0<P(E=1)<1\) and the selection probabilities are positive. Equality of the selected laws therefore implies equality of the conditional probabilities of \(Y=1\) in each such stratum.

In model zero, \(B=b\) and \(Z_2=z\) determine \(W=b\oplus z\); in model one, \(Z_2=z\) determines \(W=z\). Thus, for every \(b,d,z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \kappa_0(d,b\oplus z)=\kappa_1(d,z).
\]
Taking \(b=0\) gives \(\kappa_0(d,z)=\kappa_1(d,z)\), while taking \(b=1\) gives \(\kappa_0(d,1\oplus z)=\kappa_1(d,z)\). Hence all four values at fixed \(d\) are one number, say \(\kappa_d\).

After \(\operatorname{do}(B=0,D=d)\), selection may change the posterior law of \(W\), but the outcome probability in either model is the constant \(\kappa_d\) for both values of \(W\). Since the selection denominator is positive,
\[
 P_j(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(B=0,D=d),S=1)=\kappa_d,
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The targets are equal. The law-preservation conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\) shows that adding inactive declared coordinates cannot restore a contrast.

statements.statement: For the early-kill target, any affine fair-bit coding whose postintervention map from three independent fair latent bits to \((Y,Z_1,Z_2)\) is bijective over \(\mathbb F_2^3\) has selected target \(P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_\star=x_\star),S=1)=1/2\), provided the selector is generated from \((Z_1,Z_2)\) and an independent selector latent and the selection denominator is positive. Thus a pair of such full-rank affine codings cannot separate \(Q_{\star,x_\star}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(L\) be the vector of the three independent fair latent bits. A bijective affine map \(l\mapsto Al+c\) on \(\mathbb F_2^3\) sends the uniform law on \(\mathbb F_2^3\) to the uniform law. Therefore, under the intervention,
\[
 P(Y=y,Z_1=z_1,Z_2=z_2)=\frac18
\]
for every \((y,z_1,z_2)\). In particular, \(Y\) is fair and independent of \((Z_1,Z_2)\). If the selector is a function of \((Z_1,Z_2)\) and an exogenous input independent of \(L\), then \(Y\) is also independent of \(S\). Positivity of the selection denominator permits conditioning, and hence
\[
 P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_\star=x_\star),S=1)
 =P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_\star=x_\star))=\frac12.
\]
The conclusion applies to each member of any proposed pair in this affine class, so their targets cannot differ.

statements.statement: Let \(F_0\subset F_1\) be finite nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests in a semi-Markovian ADMG, with \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(V(F_1)\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). The positive finite-state completeness construction of Kivva et al. supplies an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), finite state spaces, and two semi-Markovian SCMs using the forest incidence that have the same strictly positive observational distribution but, at a common treatment value, have different postintervention distributions on \(R\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(H=F_1\), regarded as the semi-Markovian graph whose observed vertex set is \(V(F_1)\), and put
\[
 Z=X_N\cap V(F_1),\qquad O=R.
\]
The sets \(Z\) and \(O\) are disjoint: indeed, \(R\subseteq C=V(F_0)\) because \(F_0\) is \(R\)-rooted, while the hypothesis \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\) gives \(R\cap Z=\varnothing\). The hypothesis \(V(F_1)\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\) gives \(V(F_1)\cap Z=Z\ne\varnothing\), and
\[
 V(F_0)\cap Z=C\cap X_N\cap V(F_1)=\varnothing.
\]
By hypothesis, \(F_1\) and \(F_0\) are both \(R\)-rooted C-forests, and \(F_0\subset F_1\). Every vertex is its own ancestor via the length-zero directed path. Since \(R\cap Z=\varnothing\), those paths remain in \(H_{\overline Z}\), whence
\[
 R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{H_{\overline Z}}(R).
\]
This inclusion is proper if the source's symbol \(\subset\) is read strictly. Indeed, \(Z\ne\varnothing\), and every nonroot vertex of the finite directed forest has a unique directed path ending in \(R\). On such a path starting from any element of \(Z\), choose the last vertex \(z_*\) that belongs to \(Z\). The remaining path from \(z_*\) to \(R\) has no arrow whose head lies in \(Z\), so it survives removal of arrows into \(Z\). Thus \(z_*\in\operatorname{An}_{H_{\overline Z}}(R)\setminus R\).
Thus \(\langle F_1,F_0\rangle\) satisfies every clause of Shpitser--Pearl's Definition 7 for a hedge for \(P_z(R)\): the outer forest meets \(Z\), the inner forest avoids \(Z\), the forests are nested and have the same root set, and the root-ancestor condition holds. By \(\mathrm{lem:shpitser\text{-}pearl\text{-}ordinary\text{-}hedge\text{-}criterion}\), the ordinary causal effect \(P_z(R)\) is not identifiable in \(H\).

To instantiate the positive construction without changing its information regime, take Kivva et al.'s collection of known distributions to be the singleton \(\mathcal A=\{V(F_1)\}\). Its only known kernel is then
\[
 Q[V(F_1)]=P(V(F_1)).
\]
Kivva et al.'s Definition 3 quantifies identifiability over models having full-support observational laws. Their complete ordinary Algorithm 1 therefore reports failure for the hedge above. Equivalently, with
\[
 W=\operatorname{An}_{H[V(F_1)\setminus Z]}(R),
\]
the reduction used by that algorithm contains a single-C-component kernel \(Q[B]\), for some district \(B\subseteq W\), on which its \(\operatorname{ID\text{-}Single}\) call fails. In the proof of Kivva et al.'s Theorem 1, the choice \(\mathcal A=\{V(F_1)\}\) makes equation (4) precisely equality of the full observational law, whereas equation (5) is disagreement on this failed kernel. That proof chooses an arbitrary odd \(\kappa>4\), uses only finite alphabets, and solves its linear system with strictly positive latent weights. Kivva et al.'s Proposition 4 combines the component kernels into \(Q[W]\), and the supplementary proof of Proposition 3 transports the resulting nonidentifiability back to the causal target \(P_z(R)\) while preserving equality of the known distribution. These cited facts are recorded in \(\mathrm{lem:kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}finite\text{-}id\text{-}witness}\).

Consequently there are common finite state spaces and two semi-Markovian models \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) inducing \(H\), together with a common \(z^\dagger\in\mathcal X_Z\), such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(V(F_1)=h)
 =P_{\overline M_1}(V(F_1)=h)>0
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathcal X_{V(F_1)},
\]
but
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(R\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=z^\dagger))
 \ne
 P_{\overline M_1}(R\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=z^\dagger)).
\]
Because \(H=F_1\), these models use precisely the forest incidence. The cited construction uses \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\)-valued forest coordinates and finite product alphabets for the remaining coordinates. This proves the claim. The additional hypothesis \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) is not needed to separate the local root distribution; it is the load-bearing condition for routing that contrast to \(Y_N\) in the selected-law extension.

For an exact smallest-instance check, take the two-observed-node bow graph \(Z\to R\) and \(Z\leftrightarrow R\), with \(F_1=H\), \(F_0=\{R\}\), and a fair binary latent variable \(U\) shared by the two mechanisms. In both models let
\[
 P(Z=1\mid U=0)=\frac15,
 \qquad
 P(Z=1\mid U=1)=\frac45.
\]
For \(j=0\), set the four probabilities \(P_j(R=1\mid Z=z,U=u)\), ordered as \((z,u)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), equal to
\[
 \left(\frac25,\frac9{10},\frac9{10},\frac25\right),
\]
and for \(j=1\) set them equal to
\[
 \left(\frac35,\frac1{10},\frac1{10},\frac35\right).
\]
Independent finite private randomizers realize these kernels as recursive SCMs. Every displayed probability lies strictly between zero and one; both \(U\to Z\) and \(U\to R\) are active and the response of \(R\) changes with \(Z\), so both models induce the bow graph. Bayes' rule gives
\[
 P(U=0\mid Z=1)=\frac15,
 \qquad
 P(U=0\mid Z=0)=\frac45.
\]
Substitution in the two response tables yields
\[
 P_0(R=1\mid Z=z)=P_1(R=1\mid Z=z)=\frac12
 \quad (z=0,1),
\]
and \(P_j(Z=z)=1/2\); hence both observational laws assign probability \(1/4\) to every \((z,r)\). On the other hand,
\[
 P_0(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=1))=\frac{13}{20},
 \qquad
 P_1(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=1))=\frac7{20}.
\]
This verifies the mechanism on the smallest hedge. It is not a binary construction for arbitrary forests. The outer-treatment condition is load-bearing: if \(V(F_1)\cap X_N=\varnothing\), then \(Z=\varnothing\) in the specialization above and the target is the observed marginal \(P(R)\), which cannot differ between models sharing the full observational law.
statements.justification: This proved reduction maps each actual-edge nested forest to the ordinary hedge criterion and then invokes KivvaEtAl2022's positive finite-state completeness construction.
statements.gap: The reduction is confined to ordinary actual-edge forests; it does not lift virtual edges through selection ancestors or provide binary, rational, or executable certificates.
statements.consumer: The native separator specializes the resulting full-support ordinary countermodels to an actual terminal native forest.

statements.statement: Whenever published Algorithm 1 reaches its single-component recursion, every call chain terminates. A recursive step with fixed target \(C=D_i\) replaces \(T\) by the S-component \(T'\) containing \(D_i\) inside \(A=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(D_i)\), where \(T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T\). Hence \(\rho\) decreases strictly. The chain rooted at \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, its depth is at most \(|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most \(B_0\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \((D_i,T_i^{(0)})\). Every call keeps \(C=D_i\). Recursion occurs only when
\[
 C\subsetneq A:=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)\subsetneq T.
\]
The next enclosure is the S-component \(T'\) of \(A\) containing \(C\), whence
\[
 \varnothing\ne C\subseteq T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T,\qquad |T'|\le|T|-1.
\]
Thus each step replaces a positive entry \(|T|\) of \(\rho\) by a strictly smaller one. Equivalently, \(|T|\) decreases strictly on each chain, excluding an infinite chain. If \(|T_i^{(0)}|=m\), there are at most \(m-1\) decreases and at most \(m\) invocations. Since \(T_i^{(0)}\subseteq N_S\), depth is at most \(|N_S|\). Summing and using \(\mathrm{def:initial\text{-}call\text{-}budget}\),
\[
 \#\{\text{single-component invocations}\}
 \le\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|=B_0.
\]
Finiteness of \(G^S\) makes all bounds finite.
statements.justification: This isolates strict graph shrinkage from certificate generation.
statements.gap: It does not bound an unproved compiler.
statements.consumer: The native equivalence and executable verification theorem use it.

statements.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. There exist an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma_T\) on \(T\), two finite semi-Markovian SCMs \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) whose incidences are contained in \(G^S[T]\), the concrete local intervention \(x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}\), and an assignment \(r^\dagger\in\mathcal X_R\) such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(T=t)=P_{\overline M_1}(T=t)>0
 \quad\text{for every }t\in\mathcal X_T,
\]
and
\[
 \delta:=P_{\overline M_0}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\ne0.
\]
The signature is the finite Kivva construction, with forest-coordinate alphabets based on \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\) and finite product alphabets elsewhere. No binary, rational, or effective-encoding conclusion is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) and let \((C,T)\) be a reachable terminal failure. By \(\mathrm{lem:shedge\text{-}projects\text{-}to\text{-}hedge}\), together with the actual-incidence clause of \(\mathrm{def:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace}\), there are nested common-\(R\)-rooted C-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) with
\[
 V(F_0)=C,\qquad V(F_1)=T,
\]
all their directed and bidirected edges belonging to \(G^S[N_S]\), and
\[
 C\cap X_N=\varnothing,\qquad
 T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing,\qquad
 R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).
\]
These are exactly the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}finite\text{-}forest\text{-}countermodels}\), applied to the semi-Markovian graph \(F_1\). Hence there are an odd \(\kappa>4\), a finite signature \(\widetilde\sigma_T\), two finite semi-Markovian models \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) using only the edges of \(F_1\subseteq G^S[T]\), and a common treatment value \(z^\dagger\in\mathcal X_{X_N\cap T}\), such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(T=t)=P_{\overline M_1}(T=t)>0
 \quad\text{for every }t\in\mathcal X_T,
\]
while their postintervention laws on \(R\) at \(z^\dagger\) differ.

For each \(q\in X_N\cap T\), choose a permutation of its finite alphabet that maps \(z_q^\dagger\) to a distinguished symbol \(0\), and conjugate the structural table for \(q\) and every table receiving \(q\) by that permutation, in both models. This is a common bijective relabeling of endogenous states. Therefore it preserves equality of corresponding observational atoms, strict positivity of every atom, and inequality of the corresponding postintervention distributions. After relabeling the common intervention is
\[
 x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}.
\]
The two resulting probability measures on the finite set \(\mathcal X_R\) are unequal. Therefore there exists \(r^\dagger\in\mathcal X_R\) for which their point masses differ. Defining
\[
 \delta=
 P_{\overline M_0}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
\]
gives \(\delta\ne0\). The alphabet description is inherited from the cited Kivva construction: the forest coordinates are based on \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\), and all other coordinates are finite products. No step performs a binary reduction, chooses rational tables, or constructs an effective encoding.
statements.justification: This revalidated lemma extracts a named root-atom contrast from the repaired ordinary positive-forest carrier on an actual terminal trace.
statements.gap: Its state spaces are finite but multistate, and it makes no rational or effective-encoding claim.
statements.consumer: The selected extension carries this root contrast to the original outcome along actual treatment-avoiding paths.

statements.statement: For every finite-signature recursive augmented SCM \(\widetilde M\) whose declared parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce a subgraph of \(G^S\), \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}(\widetilde M)\) induces exactly \(G^S\). It has the same observational law and the same postintervention law under every intervention on observed vertices. In particular, strict selected-cell positivity and every intervention-before-conditioning target with positive selection denominator are preserved.
statements.proof_tex:
Order the endogenous vertices topologically. Fix every original and fresh exogenous assignment. At the first vertex, the completed function ignores all new parent and latent coordinates, so its output equals the old output. If equality holds at all earlier vertices, coordinate-constancy gives equality at the next vertex. Induction proves pointwise equality of the full endogenous vector.

The fresh factors are independent and normalized, so summing them multiplies every original atom by
\[
 \prod_{U\ \mathrm{fresh}}\sum_uP(U=u)=1.
\]
The observational laws coincide. Under an intervention, the same equations are replaced by the same constants, and the induction applies to the remaining equations; all postintervention laws coincide. Thus selected atoms, selection denominators, and defined conditional targets are preserved.

Every missing directed edge is now in a declared parent interface and every missing bidirected edge has a fresh shared factor. No unlisted incidence was added. The completed induced graph is exactly \(G^S\), and equality of laws preserves positivity.
statements.justification: This restores unused exact-graph incidences for finite multistate models without changing laws.
statements.gap: It is a representation lemma, not a separator.
statements.consumer: The native extension applies it after constructing the contrast.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, then \(G^S\) is an admissible finite childless-selector augmented ADMG for the published latent S-ID problem. For every finite signature \(\sigma\), the class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) on this restricted trace is exactly the exact-induced-graph positive compatibility class of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\). Hence native-forest traces form a subclass of the published graph instances, without restricting the SCM class on a fixed member graph.
statements.proof_tex: Clause (i) of \(\mathrm{def:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace}\) gives finiteness, acyclicity, childlessness of \(S\), and the query's disjointness and nonemptiness. These are the published graph and query premises. The definition's final sentence leaves compatibility unchanged. Unfolding \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) has exactly the graph parent interfaces, exactly the graph shared-exogenous incidences, mutually independent exogenous variables, and positive selected cells. Thus the native condition restricts only graph traces and selects a subclass of published instances. No strict-inclusion claim is made.
statements.justification: This proves that native traces remain inside the published graph setting.
statements.gap: No strict-inclusion claim is made.
statements.consumer: The native headline can reuse published soundness without changing the model class.

statements.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. Then there exist a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma\), an intervention value \(x^\dagger\in\mathcal X_X\), two models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\), and an event \(A_Y\subseteq\mathcal X_Y\) such that
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)=P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
\]
but
\[
 P_{M_0}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1)
 \ne P_{M_1}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1).
\]
Consequently \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) is false. The construction is finite and positive but is not claimed binary, rational, or executable.
statements.proof_tex:
Use \(\mathrm{lem:positive\text{-}multistate\text{-}native\text{-}forest\text{-}separator}\) and put
\[
 h(a)=P_{\overline M_0}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0)),
\]
with \(\delta=h(r^\dagger)\ne0\). For each \(r\in R\), native incidence supplies a path
\[
 \gamma_r:r=v_{r,0}\to\cdots\to v_{r,\ell_r}=y(r),
 \qquad y(r)\in Y_N,
\]
inside \(G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]\). Paths may share vertices or branches.

Augment each path vertex by one signal coordinate for every path through it. The \(r\)-signal has alphabet \(\mathcal X_r\). At its source and each later path vertex use the same randomized-response channel
\[
 K_{\epsilon,r}(z\mid u)
 =(1-\epsilon)\mathbf 1\{z=u\}+\frac{\epsilon}{|\mathcal X_r|},
 \qquad 0<\epsilon<1.
\]
Use independent finite private noises, and product channels at shared vertices. Retain the Kivva base coordinates on \(T\), and give all other base coordinates independent full-support laws. Conditional on the base vector on \(T\), all new coordinates have one common strictly positive conditional kernel. Equality and positivity of the base laws therefore imply
\[
 P_0(V=v)=P_1(V=v)>0
\]
for every augmented state \(v\).

Give all vertices in \(A_S\) identical independent full-support mechanisms, and make \(S\) an independent fair bit while ignoring its declared parents. Then
\[
 P_j(V=v,S=1)=\frac12P_j(V=v)>0,\qquad
 P_j(V=v\mid S=1)=P_j(V=v),
\]
so the selected laws agree.

Let \(L=\sum_{r\in R}(\ell_r+1)\). Couple every channel as exact copying with probability \(1-\epsilon\) and uniform redrawing with probability \(\epsilon\). All terminal signals equal their root inputs with probability at least \((1-\epsilon)^L\). If \(A_Y\) is the event that the terminal signal tuple equals \(r^\dagger\), then for \(j=0,1\),
\[
 \left|P_j(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_{\overline M_j}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\right|
 \le1-(1-\epsilon)^L.
\]
Here \(x^\dagger\) uses Kivva's zero levels on \(X_N\cap T\) and fixed values elsewhere. The paths avoid \(X_N\), so intervention cuts no signal channel. Choose \(\epsilon\) with
\[
 2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}<|\delta|.
\]
The triangle inequality yields
\[
 |P_0(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_1(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))|
 \ge|\delta|-2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}>0.
\]
Independence of \(S\) persists after intervention, so conditioning on \(S=1\) changes neither target.

All used forest and routing edges are actual edges of \(G^S\); the premodels induce subgraphs of \(G^S\). Apply \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}\). By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\), the completed models induce exactly \(G^S\) and preserve the equal positive selected law and target contrast. They lie in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\). This one finite-signature pair falsifies \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\).
statements.justification: This constructs equal positive selected laws and a nonzero original-outcome event contrast.
statements.gap: Its channel construction requires native actual edges.
statements.consumer: It proves the failure direction of the native headline.

statements.statement:
Let \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) hold. Then published Algorithm 1 succeeds on \((G^S,X,Y)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds. On success, for every finite signature \(\sigma\), every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M),
\]
with the outer conditional evaluated at \(x_S\) and every recursive kernel at \(x_N\). On terminal failure, \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) supplies one finite multistate signature and two exact-graph models with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. No binary, rational, or executable failure certificate is claimed.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume throughout that \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds.  By \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace\text{-}subclass}\), \(G^S\) is an admissible finite childless-selector augmented ADMG for published Algorithm~1, and, for each finite signature \(\sigma\), its compatible models are exactly the members of \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\).

First suppose that Algorithm~1 succeeds.  Fix a finite signature \(\sigma\), an intervention value \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and a model \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}cell\text{-}positivity}\),
\[
 P_M(V=v,S=1)>0
 \qquad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j.
\]
Consequently, every marginal cell of the selected law that occurs as a denominator in the outer conditional or in a recursively extracted selected kernel is a finite sum of positive cells and is therefore positive.  In particular,
\[
 P_M(X_S=x_S,S=1)
 =\sum_{v:\,v|_{X_S}=x_S}P_M(V=v,S=1)>0,
\]
so the outer conditional at \(X_S=x_S\) is defined.  The same summation argument applies to every conditioning configuration used by the successful recursive factors evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\).  Moreover, \(\mathrm{lem:target\text{-}support}\) gives
\[
 P_M(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))>0,
\]
so the intervention-before-conditioning target is defined.  The hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}latent\text{-}sid\text{-}soundness}\) therefore apply, and, pointwise for every \(y\in\prod_{v\in Y}\mathcal X_v\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)(y)
 =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)(y).
\]
This is precisely the displayed success conclusion, with the evaluation conventions fixed by \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\).

To deduce graphwise identification, take arbitrary \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) satisfying
\[
 P_{M_0,\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\sigma}^S.
\]
Applying the preceding equality first to \(M_0\) and then to \(M_1\) yields
\[
 \Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_0)
 =\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M_0,\sigma}^S)
 =\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M_1,\sigma}^S)
 =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_1).
\]
Because \(\sigma\), \(x\), \(M_0\), and \(M_1\) were arbitrary within one common signature, \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\) implies \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\).

Conversely, suppose that Algorithm~1 does not succeed.  Clause~(ii) of \(\mathrm{def:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace}\) says that its initial selected d-separation check passes.  Hence nonsuccess occurs, if at all, in a single-component recursive chain.  By \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\), the chain rooted at each \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, every chain has depth at most \(|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most
\[
 B_0=\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|<\infty.
\]
Therefore a finite execution that does not return the success branch reaches an actual terminal failed call \((C,T)\).  The hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) now hold.  That lemma supplies one finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma\), one value \(x^\dagger\in\mathcal X_X\), models
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma),
\]
and an event \(A_Y\subseteq\mathcal X_Y\) such that, pointwise on \(\mathcal X_V\),
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)
 =P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)>0,
\]
whereas
\[
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_0)(A_Y)
 \ne
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1)(A_Y).
\]
The latter inequality implies that the two finite probability distributions \(\Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_0)\) and \(\Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1)\) are unequal, while the preceding pointwise equality says that their selected observational laws coincide.  Thus this single within-\(\widetilde\sigma\) pair violates the implication quantified in \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\), and
\[
 \neg\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y).
\]
We have proved that success implies identification and that failure implies nonidentification; equivalently, Algorithm~1 succeeds if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds.  The converse used the terminal selected extension only under \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\); it makes no assertion about virtual-edge traces, initial-check failures, binary or rational witnesses, or an executable failure compiler.

statements.statement: Let \(H\) be a finite semi-Markovian graph, let \(Z\) and \(O\) be sets of observed vertices, and let \(F\) and \(F'\) be \(R\)-rooted C-forests. If \(V(F)\cap Z\ne\varnothing\), \(V(F')\cap Z=\varnothing\), \(F'\subseteq F\), and \(R\subset\operatorname{An}_{H_{\overline Z}}(O)\), then \(F,F'\) form a hedge for \(P_z(O)\), and \(P_z(O)\) is not identifiable from the observational law in \(H\).

statements.statement: Let \(H\) be a finite semi-Markovian causal graph and let \(Z,O\) be disjoint observed vertex sets. Under the positive-model definition \(P_M(h)>0\) for every observed assignment \(h\), ordinary Algorithm 1 is sound and complete. When it returns failure for \(P_z(O)\), the constructive necessity argument may be carried out with an odd integer \(\kappa>4\) and common finite state spaces, and it gives two semi-Markovian structural equation models inducing \(H\), with the same full-support observational law, but with different distributions \(P_z(O)\) at some common value \(z\). The construction uses \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\)-valued forest coordinates and finite product coordinates; Proposition 4 combines the failed component kernels, and the supplementary proof of Proposition 3 transfers the resulting kernel disagreement to the stated causal effect.

source.verbatim_statement: Definition 3 (identifiability). Suppose X and Y are two disjoint subsets of V. The causal effect of X on Y is said to be identifiable from G if for any x and y, P^M_x(y) is uniquely computable from P^M(V) in any SEM M in M+(G). Proposition 4. Suppose S1,...,Sl are the c-components of S. Q[S] is g-identifiable from (A,G) if and only if Q[Si] is g-identifiable from (A,G) for all i. Theorem 1. Suppose S is a single c-component. Q[S] is g-identifiable from (A,G) if and only if there exists A in A such that S is contained in A and Q[S] is identifiable from G[A]. statements.statement: For every finite childless-selector augmented ADMG \(G^S\), including graphs whose terminal S-Hedges require virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching selection ancestors and instances failing the initial d-separation check, does published Algorithm 1 succeed if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds? Equivalently, can every failure be converted into a finite-signature exact-graph pair with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets? The native-forest theorem answers this only on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\).
statements.proof_tex: The equivalence is proved when the initial d-separation check passes and every terminal forest is native in \(G^S[N_S]\). Projection geometry holds for arbitrary terminal S-Hedges, but a common-positive-law inverse realization for virtual edges and an independent initial-failure compiler are absent.
statements.justification: This faithfully preserves the unrestricted conjecture.
statements.gap: Virtual-edge and initial-failure countermodel construction remain open.
statements.consumer: It is the frontier beyond the restricted theorem.

statements.statement: Whenever the initial selected d-separation check of published Algorithm 1 fails, can one effectively choose \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and construct \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) with rational finite tables such that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\)? The definition of \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) names this desired output but does not prove that the compiler exists.
statements.proof_tex: Coordinate-constant exactification preserves any raw separating pair once supplied, and checker acceptance would certify the required same-law target separation. The frozen \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) construction, however, cites an intended fully observed necessity construction without deriving finite rational tables or accepted evidence.
statements.justification: This preserves the independent initial-failure compiler as open.
statements.gap: No finite rational accepted pair has been constructed.
statements.consumer: Both unrestricted completeness and total compilation require it.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) be made total by two effective finite-rational compilers: one for failure of the initial selected d-separation check and one for every terminal recursive S-Hedge, each returning an accepted exact-graph \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair? A positive answer requires both the independent \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) compiler and the compositional inverse lift with noncancelling outcome contrast; graph-recursion termination and checker verification alone do not construct either pair.
statements.proof_tex: The graph recursion has a strict cardinality-decrease bound and every supplied rational certificate has a sound finite checker. Total compilation remains open because neither the initial-failure compiler nor the arbitrary virtual-edge terminal compiler is proved.
statements.justification: This records the missing operational endpoint.
statements.gap: Both failure compilers are required.
statements.consumer: A total implementation depends on resolving it.

statements.statement: Does there exist \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\) and \(E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1}\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\) such that the exact checker accepts, their realized models have the same strictly positive selected law on every cell of \(\{0,1\}^{V_\star}\), and \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,0}\rrbracket)\ne Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,1}\rrbracket)\)? The known support-deficient pair has targets \(1/2\) and \(5/8\), but does not answer this positive-binary question.
statements.proof_tex: An exact rational support-deficient pair is known: both models have \(D=B\), \(Y=B\oplus Z_2\), and the same selected law on their common support, while at \(\operatorname{do}(B=0,D=0)\) their selected targets are \(1/2\) and \(5/8\). It fails strict selected-cell positivity. Independent smoothing forces equality of the relevant outcome kernels, and full-rank affine fair-bit codings force both targets to \(1/2\).
statements.justification: This is the smallest unresolved positive-binary virtual-edge stress test.
statements.gap: The exact separating pair is support deficient and two natural smoothing classes erase the contrast.
statements.consumer: It is a necessary base case for any binary rational universal lift.

sampling_model.design: The population theorem is a graphwise identification result restricted to \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\). Within each finite signature it uses one exact selected observational law and compares only augmented SCMs with that same signature whose declared parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce exactly \(G^S\). There is no sampling approximation or randomization design in the theorem.
sampling_model.units: A unit is a recursive augmented SCM on a finite childless-selector ADMG \(G^S\), with \(2\le |\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for each substantive variable and binary \(S\). Exogenous variables are mutually independent and may enter several mechanisms. The proved terminal-failure witness uses one finite multistate signature and is not claimed binary, rational, or effectively encoded.
sampling_model.treatment: For each signature, \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and the intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\) is applied to the SCM before conditioning on \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Within each signature, every cell \(v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\) has \(P_M(V=v,S=1)>0\), and the queried postintervention selection event has positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Within each signature the input is the exact law \(P_{M,\sigma}^S=P_M(V\mid S=1)\); estimation of Eq. 23 is a separate statistical problem.

estimand_functional: \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_\sigma^S)(y)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal X_W} P_\sigma^S(Y_S=y_S,W=w\mid X_S=x_S)\sum_{d_{D\setminus Y_N}\in\mathcal X_{D\setminus Y_N}}\prod_{D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)}Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[D_i](d_i\mid y_S,w,x_S,d_{D\setminus D_i})\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For exact childless-selector augmented SCMs, Algorithm 1 and Eq. 23 are sound, while the published paper leaves graphwise completeness open.
The fully observed augmented-DAG S-ID criterion is sound and complete.
Ordinary semi-Markovian ID is complete, and an ordinary nested C-forest hedge certifies nonidentifiability.
The Tian--Pearl identification recursion is complete for ordinary semi-Markovian causal effects.
Conditioning an SCM on latent selection preserves causal semantics and commutes with intervention outside the selector's ancestors.
Ordinary positive-model identification is complete and its necessity proof constructs finite full-support countermodels from failed ordinary ID instances.
Conditional generalized identification extends the positive general-identification framework but does not directly state the ordinary native-forest specialization used here.
A general identification algorithm combines multiple input distributions generated under systematic selection regimes for data-fusion queries.
Discrete causal questions with selection admit sharp polynomial-program bounds over canonical response types.
Full-population ATE recovery from selected data has a necessary-and-sufficient distribution-class condition under unconfoundedness.
A two-sample Mendelian-randomization analysis studies HbA1c and white-matter brain aging in differently selected UK Biobank samples.

tldr: For graphs satisfying \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), published latent S-ID Algorithm 1 succeeds if and only if the selected causal query is graphwise identifiable over the full positive exact-graph augmented-SCM class, with models compared only within one finite signature. Success returns Abouei et al.'s Eq. 23 functional. A terminal recursive failure contains an ordinary hedge whose edges are actual edges of \(G^S[N_S]\); Shpitser--Pearl's hedge criterion and KivvaEtAl2022's positive finite-state construction give a full-support multistate separator, and a common randomized-response routing plus finite exactification yields two exact-graph models with the same strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. Separate finite rank bounds certify graph recursion, and the rational checker is sound for any supplied certificate. The result does not construct binary or rational failure witnesses. Universal virtual-edge completeness, the positive-binary two-virtual-edge separator, initial selected-d-separation failure construction, exact-rational inverse lifting, and total success-or-certificate compilation remain open. The UK Biobank component remains only a conditional two-selector feasibility audit.

project_justification.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID proves Algorithm 1 sound and leaves completeness open. Ordinary hedge completeness alone does not solve terminal failures whose projected bidirected edges must be realized through shared or branching ancestors of \(S\), because such realizations can change every selected atom and its normalizer. KivvaEtAl2022 supplies a positive finite-state construction for ordinary identification failures, but not a selected-law inverse lift through those virtual edges.
project_justification.niche: The predicate \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) isolates the terminal traces for which the nested common-root forests can be chosen using actual directed and bidirected edges of \(G^S[N_S]\). On this class the ordinary positive-forest construction can be used before adding a common selection mechanism and actual-edge root-to-outcome channels.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the missing converse on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\). It verifies the Shpitser--Pearl hedge clauses for each terminal native forest, invokes KivvaEtAl2022 for finite full-support ordinary countermodels, extracts a nonzero root-atom contrast, routes it to \(Y_N\) through common full-support randomized-response channels on treatment-avoiding actual paths, and exactifies inert interfaces without changing the equal selected law or target contrast. Combined with published soundness, this gives the success-if-and-only-if theorem and Eq. 23 on success. Independent results bound the graph recursion and verify any supplied rational certificate, without claiming a binary, rational, or executable failure constructor.

related_work: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID defines latent subpopulation S-ID, Algorithm 1, S-components, S-Hedges, and Eq. 23, proves soundness, and leaves completeness open. This paper advances that frontier only on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\): it does not settle unrestricted terminal traces or initial selected-d-separation failure. ShpitserPearl2006 provides Definition 7's ordinary hedge criterion and Theorem 4's nonidentifiability implication. KivvaEtAl2022, not KivvaEtAl2023 Appendix A.1.1, provides the positive finite-state ordinary-ID substrate used here; the new work is the reduction from an actual-edge terminal S-Hedge to that substrate, followed by selected-law extension, actual-edge root-to-outcome routing, and inert exactification. KivvaEtAl2023 concerns conditional generalized identification and does not directly state this ordinary-forest specialization. HuangValtorta2008 and TianPearl2002 provide the ordinary recursive-identification and district-factorization background. AboueiEtAl2024SID is used only for the known no-latent DAG regression check. ChenZoeterMooij2024 explains selection conditioning as an SCM transformation but does not supply a common-selected-law inverse countermodel lift. RichardsonEtAl2017 supplies nested Markov and district-kernel language useful for describing recursive kernels and full-graph extension; it does not prove the selected-law converse. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 studies semiparametric inference after hidden-variable identification and is relevant only to separating this population identification result from downstream estimation; it supplies no completeness claim. LeeGhassamiShpitser2024 uses multiple systematic-selection inputs rather than one full selected law. DuarteEtAl2024AutoBounds addresses optimization-based discrete partial identification, not singleton collapse at S-ID success. The UK Biobank citations motivate a conditional two-selector feasibility audit only; no empirical effect or unconditional fusion claim is made.
interpretation: The native theorem marks the boundary at which terminal latent S-ID failure already contains an ordinary hedge inside the selection-nonancestor graph. At that boundary, an ordinary positive separator can be passed through a common independent selector and sufficiently accurate full-support channels without canceling its root contrast. When a terminal forest uses virtual edges through ancestors of \(S\), this argument no longer controls the selected-law normalizer, so the universal converse remains unresolved.
technical_internal_limitation: The proof requires actual-edge nested forests on every reachable terminal failure. It does not realize projected virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching ancestors of \(S\). Accordingly, unrestricted graphwise completeness, the positive-binary two-virtual-edge separation problem, the initial selected-d-separation failure constructor, exact-rational inverse lifting, and total success-or-certificate compilation all remain open. The proved Kivva reduction is finite and full-support but multistate; no binary reduction, rational parameter choice, or executable constructor follows from it. The rational checker theorem is only a sound verification result conditional on a certificate being supplied.
honest_scope: The headline theorem is an if-and-only-if result only for finite childless-selector queries satisfying \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\). The compatible class is the full positive recursive augmented-SCM class whose declared observed-parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce exactly \(G^S\), and observational equivalence compares models only within one finite signature. On success, Eq. 23 is evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\) in the outer conditional and at \(X_N=x_N\) in every recursive selected kernel. On a terminal native failure, the proof supplies one finite multistate exact-graph pair with a common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. It does not supply a binary or rational pair. Coordinate-constant exactification preserves the relevant laws under the declared-interface graph convention. Graph-recursion bounds and sound finite checking of a supplied rational certificate are separate proved properties; they do not make the failure branch executable. Universal virtual-edge completeness, the positive-binary two-virtual-edge separator, initial-check failure construction, exact-rational inverse lifting, and total compilation remain open. The no-bidirected-edge result is only a published-case regression check. The UK Biobank component is conditional on a specified two-selector graph and a nonempty feasibility fiber; absent two exact-graph models in that same fiber with unequal targets, it reports only unmet assumptions or an inconclusive audit, not data-compatible nonidentification.
